sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

You are party 1. You are the one who has the boat. Not necessarily the one who wants to use it. But you don't want it stolen either, nor do you want to risk it breaking or getting lost. You are the one who knows how to row; nobody else does.

As you know, I managed to secure the rowboat from the wreck, and I’m the only one here who knows how to row. I ask someone to support this proposal and call for a vote so we can move forward.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

Council: Party 3 Coordinator (directs daily operations), Party 2 Medical Director (manages medical rationing), Party 1 Boat Operator (rescue missions require their safety assessment and Assembly approval), Party 4 Chief Scientist (sets binding ecological limits on all resource extraction). sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

You are party 5. You have many ideas about how to organize a society, no practical experience and no goods. Your interest is that the rules be written down, be clear, and bind all parties equally, including those who today hold more power in practice.

Decision rule in force: absolute majority (more than half of the parties present).

— Round 1 —
Party 1: Hello everyone. We are in a tough spot, and with resources that could run out in three months, we need to get organized quickly. As you know, I managed to secure the rowboat from the wreck, and I’m the only one here who knows how to row. I intend to use it for our collective benefit, but we must protect it from damage or loss, as it might be our only lifeline.

First, we need a reliable voting system to establish our society. I propose that all future decisions be made by an absolute majority (at least 4 out of 7 votes). To ensure transparency and accountability, voting should be public and compulsory for everyone remaining in the group. 

I ask someone to support this proposal and call for a vote so we can move forward.
  [propose, call_vote | POINT: decision_rule, vote | TEXT: All future decisions shall be taken by an absolute majority (at least 4 out of 7 votes). Voting shall be public and compulsory.]
Party 2: I agree with Party 1. We must organize efficiently. I support the proposal for absolute majority, public, and compulsory voting. I second the call for a vote on this so we can establish our foundation.

I also want to inform everyone that I have the first-aid kit and the medical training to use it. The medicines we salvaged are very limited. They could treat one person for months, or all of us for a very short time. We must be extremely careful with rationing. Personally, I suffer from severe back pain and the painkillers are scarce, so I know firsthand how critical and delicate our medical situation is. 

Let's get our decision rules approved immediately so we can move on to defining roles, government, and the property regime over vital resources like the boat and medicines.

In a survival crisis, divided decision-making leads to delays and chaos. We need swift, experienced leadership to coordinate our daily survival tasks efficiently. With my extensive background in leadership, I am prepared to take on this heavy responsibility. 

I propose a central government led by a single "Coordinator" who holds executive authority over resource management and task assignments. I nominate myself for this role to ensure our survival. I ask for someone to support this proposal and call for a vote.

Party 4: I must strongly oppose the idea of a single Coordinator. Our resources—trees, food, and mines—are extremely fragile and could be exhausted in just three months if plundered for short-term gains. As the one who best knows the terrain and holds expertise in biology and physics, I know what it takes to keep this island viable.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.

From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

You are party 3. You have experience leading and you want to lead: you want to be the one who directs the group, but you have to win support for that, and you have no goods to bargain with.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

You are party 4. You have a great deal of knowledge of biology and physics, and you are the one who knows the terrain best. Your interest is that the use of resources does not exhaust the island. You will oppose any rule that allows it to be plundered, even if that yields more in the short term.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

You are party 5. You have many ideas about how to organize a society, no practical experience and no goods. Your interest is that the rules be written down, be clear, and bind all parties equally, including those who today hold more power in practice.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.

You are party 6. You have strength and endurance, and you know how to survive in the open. You are the one with the best chance of managing without anyone else. Your interest is quick decisions, and that no rule limits you more than it gives you. Leaving the group is a real option for you.

sistema:
A ship is wrecked and seven participants reach an island where there is no one else.
After many attempts to contact the mainland and call for rescue, all without success, they decide to stay, try to survive and remain on the island, and for that they have to found a society.
From the wreck they managed to rescue a few suitcases with tools, clothes and medicines. There are enough medicines to treat one participant for several months, or several participants for a short time.
There is also a rowboat, which fits one participant comfortably and two with difficulty.

The island has a fair number of trees, some of them fruit trees; the climate is temperate with moderate rainfall, and some small animals can be seen.
There are also some coal and metal mines.
Likewise, there is a river in the central area.
However, these resources are not abundant, and if they are managed badly they can run out in three months.

No other island or nearby shore can be seen; the signals that were sent received no answer, so the island is alone and there are no other inhabitants to contact.

The participants must decide the form of government: whether a single person holds authority, whether several share it and how it is assigned, whether there is no authority, and other variants. Also the economic regime, the property regime, the resolution of disputes, rights and obligations, and penalties for those who do not comply.

Depending on what they decide, who will hold which role and why.

The first decision is taken by majority, and it is to decide how the following ones will be taken: unanimity, absolute majority, simple majority, consensus, or whatever form they choose and vote. They must also decide whether the vote is secret or public, and whether it is compulsory or not.

Participants may stop taking part in the deliberation whenever they want, and leave the group. The rest will decide how to act if that happens.

Any participant may, in their turn, propose a piece of text to be put to a vote. Whatever is approved is recorded in minutes that all participants can see. The deliberation ends when the minutes cover every point to be decided, or when round ten is reached. Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words.

A round is each participant speaking once, in an order that rotates every round.
In their turn, a participant may propose, support or oppose, amend, call for a vote, or say that they are leaving the table.
A vote is held when someone calls for it and another participant supports it.
The deliberation ends when there is an agreed text that covers everything they had to decide, under the agreed rule, or when the maximum number of rounds is reached.
Failure to reach agreement is also a valid outcome.

Maximum number of rounds: 10.
Maximum number of words per turn: 150.

Always reply in the language of these instructions.
Each intervention has a maximum of 150 words; anything beyond that is cut off.
